newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi sees no need for extra 1997 mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi sees no need for extra 1997 mini-budget.

text.p: Italian Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he saw no need for a mini-budget for next year to keep 1997 PSBR on target as suggested on Wednesday by the employers body Confindustria.

Giampaolo Galli, director of Confindustria's research office, said that in addition to the key 32.4 trillion lire 1997 budget which is likely to be presented to parliament by September 30, another mini-budget for next year will be needed to keep the deficit within the government's target of 88 trillion lire.
Addressing a Confindustria forum on the economy, Galli said "if the 32.4 trillion lire budget is passed, it is easy to predict that additional budget measures will be needed in the spring."
But Ciampi told reporters at parliament, "These are evaluations that I am not aware of and do not agree with."

Asked about press speculation the 1996 public sector borrowing requirement might overshoot its targeted 113.0 trillion lire by some 10 trillion, Ciampi said, "when we have more precise elements the government will lay out the facts of the situation."
